:::{#thm-mutual-information-nonnegative}
#### Mutual information is nonnegative

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$ and $Y$
with finite entropies, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

$$I(X; Y) \ge 0.$$

Equality holds exactly when $X$ and $Y$ are
[independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt).

:::

::: {.proof}

Let $p(x, y)$ be the joint mass function, with marginals $p(x)$ and $p(y)$, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
and let $b$ be the base of the logarithm. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
Every $t > 0$ satisfies $\ln t \le t - 1$, with equality only at $t = 1$.
Apply it to $t = p(x) \, p(y) / p(x, y)$ for each pair with $p(x, y) > 0$.
By @thm-mutual-information-kl,

$$
\begin{aligned}
-I(X; Y) \, \ln b
&= \sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \ln \frac{p(x) \, p(y)}{p(x, y)} \\
&\le \sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \sb{\frac{p(x) \, p(y)}{p(x, y)} - 1} \\
&= \sum_{x, y} p(x) \, p(y) - \sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \\
&\le 1 - 1 \\
&= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first sum in the third line runs over the pairs with $p(x, y) > 0$, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so it is at most $\sum_{x, y} p(x) \, p(y) = 1$ over all pairs,
which gives the fourth line.
Hence $I(X; Y) \ge 0$.

Equality holds exactly when both inequalities are equalities. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
The first is an equality exactly when $p(x) \, p(y) = p(x, y)$ for every pair with $p(x, y) > 0$.
The second is an equality exactly when no pair has $p(x, y) = 0$ and $p(x) \, p(y) > 0$.
Together they say $p(x, y) = p(x) \, p(y)$ for every pair,
which is independence.
Each inequality is an equality exactly under its condition, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so independence is both necessary and sufficient for $I(X; Y) = 0$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::
